title: Zooplankton responses to ocean alkalinity enhancement under contrasting food web conditions
content:
Abstract
Ocean alkalinity enhancement (OAE) is a carbon dioxide removal strategy attracting rapidly growing research interest. However, few studies have investigated its environmental impacts on plankton communities spanning multiple trophic levels, or centered on metazoan zooplankton, key link in the flow of energy from primary producers to higher consumers including fishes. Here, we investigated plankton food webs, up to larval and juvenile fishes, under OAE in coastal Norway. Using mesocosms, we applied CO2-unequilibrated alkalinity (0 to + 600 µmol kg−1, corresponding to a pH range from 8.1 to 8.7) under two mineral scenarios (lime- and silicate-inspired). Metazoan zooplankton properties linking to food web structure, stability, and productivity were monitored over 54 days, including a nutrient-poor phase followed by a nutrient-rich phase with high predation. Despite strong chemical perturbations, zooplankton remained unaffected throughout the study. During the first phase, minimal impacts over 20 days of exposure suggest physiological resilience, and the limited propagation of OAE effects on prey nutritional value indicates that food limitation likely remained the dominant control of zooplankton. During the second phase, unexpectedly large fish assemblages likely suppressed the zooplankton, masking possible OAE effects despite prolonged exposure and stronger impacts on their prey and on the predators themselves. Future studies need to investigate the longer-term effects of OAE on zooplankton, and clarify if productivity modulates the propagation of bottom-up responses to lime- and silicate-OAE under more moderate predation.
